verdict.rationale: Gusto publishes a per-endpoint API reference (e.g. time-off decline, webhook subscription create, webhooks health check, webhook verify) and its own Postman collections for each API version, which give developers runnable requests. However, nothing in the evidence shows the reference itself is interactive, such as an in-browser 'try it' console or runnable code samples on the reference pages. Missing for 10: evidence of in-page interactive request execution, runnable code examples embedded in the reference, and independent hands-on corroboration.
